fact: Claude Code subagent model precedence: per-call Agent `model` > agent frontmatter `model` > CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL > session model. Since v2.1.251 the env var is only a default; forcing it needs CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 (v2.1.257+).
recommendation: Set phase defaults in agent frontmatter; use per-call `model` only for escalation; document min Claude Code 2.1.251.

fact: Plugin agents are namespaced `metaswarm:<name>` with lowest priority; project agent names cannot contain ':', so a project file can never shadow a plugin agent and there is no per-project model override for plugin agents.
recommendation: Generate project agents as .claude/agents/metaswarm-<role>.md (bin/metaswarm-agents.sh) and spawn via the roleType() rule: metaswarm-<role> if present, else metaswarm:<role>. New .claude/agents/ dirs need a session restart.

fact: CodeRabbit reviews incrementally and never re-reviews a commit it already reviewed: '@coderabbitai review' is a no-op then. '@coderabbitai full review' re-reviews the whole PR from scratch, but neither is guaranteed to clear an earlier CHANGES_REQUESTED. Included-review limits (2 here) can skip a push until the window resets.
recommendation: Use '@coderabbitai full review' when a fresh pass is needed. To clear a stale CHANGES_REQUESTED, dismiss that specific review; use '@coderabbitai approve' only after every CodeRabbit finding is addressed, because it resolves ALL CodeRabbit threads and can bypass the unresolved-thread check. A rate-limited push is not reviewed when capacity returns on its own: check '@coderabbitai rate limit', then request '@coderabbitai review' once capacity is back (the wait varies from minutes to over half an hour). On-demand reviews cost money, so ask first.

fact: bd (1.0.4-1.3.4): `bd prime` has no --work-type/--keywords/--files flags and never reads .beads/knowledge; `bd sync` is missing in 1.0.4 (back in 1.2.1 as pull+push); `bd compact` squashes Dolt history while `bd admin compact --analyze/--apply` summarizes closed issues with no API key (only --auto needs one) but, like every `bd admin` command, requires server mode (`bd init --server`) and is unavailable in the default embedded mode; `bd stats` aliases `bd status`.
recommendation: Use `/prime` for metaswarm knowledge, `bd dolt push/pull` (only if a Dolt remote is configured) instead of `bd sync`, and verify any bd invocation with `<sub> --help` on both bd 1.0.4 and the latest; tests/deps/test-dependency-drift.sh guards the removed forms.

provenance.reference: #62 research against checksum-verified bd 1.3.4 and installed 1.0.4
PR #71 CodeRabbit review; verified in cmd/bd/admin.go v1.0.4 and v1.3.4

fact: Node's `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json','utf-8'))` rejects a UTF-8 byte-order mark (added by some Windows editors), while `require('./package.json')` strips it. Switching to JSON.parse to detect parse errors made valid BOM files block pushes.
recommendation: To tell 'no script' from 'package.json won't parse', keep `require(path.resolve('package.json'))` inside try/catch and exit with a distinct code on error.

fact: GitHub rulesets (POST repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets): a required_status_checks context is the Actions job's `name:`; `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` targets the default branch; rulesets add to branch protection and other rulesets without replacing them; with no bypass_actors they also reject direct pushes, admins included; private repos on GitHub Free can't use rulesets or branch protection.
recommendation: Add required checks with a named ruleset (idempotent: look it up by name first) rather than PUT branch protection, which replaces existing rules. Tell users that direct pushes stop working and the setup commit should land via a PR.
